proofs.proof_tex:
List the algebraically independent source coordinates as
\[
 u=(u_1,\ldots,u_N)=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}}),
 \qquad N=|D|+|B|+n,
\]
and list the distinct covariance outputs as
\[
 s(u)=\bigl(\phi_G(\sigma_{ij}):i\leq j\bigr).
\]
Thus \(L=\mathbb C(u)\) and, by the definition of \(K_G\),
\[
 K_G=\mathbb C(s(u)).
\]
Let \(J_s\) be the Jacobian of \(s\) with respect to \(u\), and let \(J_{s,e}\) be obtained by adjoining to \(J_s\) the row \(\nabla_u\lambda_e\). Put
\[
 \rho=\operatorname{rank}_{L}J_s,
 \qquad
 \rho_e=\operatorname{rank}_{L}J_{s,e}.
\]
The Jacobian--transcendence-rank lemma gives
\[
 \rho=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G,
 \qquad
 \rho_e=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e).
\]
Adjoining one row changes rank by at most one, so \(\rho_e-\rho\in\{0,1\}\). Moreover,
\[
 \lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G(\lambda_e)
 =\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}K_G
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \rho_e=\rho.
\]
By the definition of \(d_e(G)\), this is equivalent to \(d_e(G)<\infty\). Hence the two generic ranks decide the required dichotomy. On the algebraic branch, the established orientation upper bound additionally gives
\[
 d_e(G)\leq 2^{|D|-n+2}\leq 2^{k+1}.
\]
No step of this rank comparison constructs the minimal polynomial or its degree.

Suppose instead that \(\rho_e=\rho+1\). Then \(\lambda_e\) is transcendental over \(K_G\), so the homomorphism
\[
 K_G[t]\longrightarrow L,\qquad t\longmapsto\lambda_e,
\]
is injective. The incidence-localization theorem states that \(A_K\) is an integral \(K_G\)-algebra with fraction field \(L\). Therefore the induced morphism
\[
 \operatorname{Spec}A_K\longrightarrow\mathbb A^1_{K_G}
\]
has dense image: the closure of its image is cut out by the kernel of \(K_G[t]\to A_K\), and this kernel is zero because \(A_K\hookrightarrow L\). Its source has positive dimension because its function field contains the transcendental element \(\lambda_e\). Thus a rank transcript certifying \(\rho_e=\rho+1\), together with the injective incidence chart from \(A_K\), is precisely a valid \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\).

It remains to justify the randomized construction and its cost. Acyclicity implies \(\Lambda^n=0\), and hence
\[
 (I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=I_n+\Lambda+\cdots+\Lambda^{n-1}.
\]
Consequently every coordinate of \(s(u)\), and every entry of \(J_s\) and \(J_{s,e}\), has a straight-line circuit of size polynomial in \(n\) and total degree polynomial in \(n\). Perform fraction-free Gaussian elimination on both Jacobians. Whenever a prospective pivot circuit must be classified as zero or nonzero, apply independent source-parametric polynomial identity tests. At a successful evaluation, ordinary elimination supplies the pivot rows and columns and therefore an explicit nonzero minor. Continuing elimination supplies a transcript for the asserted rank; on the transcendental branch the transcript includes a nonzero \((\rho+1)\)-minor of \(J_{s,e}\) while the corresponding elimination of \(J_s\) stops at rank \(\rho\).

There are only polynomially many tests and every cleared pivot numerator has degree and circuit size polynomial in \(n\). Choose each sampling set large enough, or repeat the tests independently, so that the Schwartz--Zippel bound makes the failure probability of each test at most \(\delta/M\), where \(M\) is the number of tests. The union bound then makes the total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). The field elements, pivot indices, minors, and elimination transcripts have total length
\[
 \operatorname{poly}(n,\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Since \(n\geq2\) and \(k\geq0\), this quantity is bounded by \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\). This proves the stated algorithmic dichotomy and its dominance certificate.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(F=\mathbb C(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\), let \(f_1,\ldots,f_m,g\in F\), and let \(J_f\) and \(J_{f,g}\) be their Jacobian matrices with respect to \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\). Then
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{F}J_f=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(f_1,\ldots,f_m)
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{rank}_{F}J_{f,g}=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(f_1,\ldots,f_m,g).
\]
In particular, \(g\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb C(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\) if and only if the two ranks are equal.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Write \(E=\mathbb C(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\), and choose a maximal algebraically independent subfamily \(f_{i_1},\ldots,f_{i_r}\). Because the characteristic is zero, every element of \(E\) is separably algebraic over \(E_0=\mathbb C(f_{i_1},\ldots,f_{i_r})\). If \(a\in E\) has minimal polynomial \(P(T)\in E_0[T]\), differentiating \(P(a)=0\) gives
\[
 P'(a)\,da=-\sum_j \frac{\partial P}{\partial f_{i_j}}(a)\,df_{i_j}.
\]
Separability gives \(P'(a)\neq0\), so \(da\) lies in the \(E\)-span of \(df_{i_1},\ldots,df_{i_r}\). Conversely, algebraic independence of the selected family identifies \(E_0\) with a rational function field; the coordinate derivations \(\partial/\partial f_{i_j}\) show that \(df_{i_1},\ldots,df_{i_r}\) are linearly independent in \(\Omega_{E_0/\mathbb C}\). Since every characteristic-zero field extension is separable, their images remain independent after extension of scalars to \(F\). Hence
\[
 \dim_F\operatorname{span}_F\{df_1,\ldots,df_m\}=r
 =\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}E.
\]
Under the standard basis \(dx_1,\ldots,dx_N\) of \(\Omega_{F/\mathbb C}\), the coefficient rows of these differentials are exactly the rows of \(J_f\), proving the first equality. Applying the same argument to the family \(f_1,\ldots,f_m,g\) proves the second. Finally, adjoining \(g\) leaves transcendence degree unchanged exactly when \(g\) is algebraic over \(E\), which proves the last assertion.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), and suppose that a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is supplied. If its total straight-line-program length is \(s\) and its maximum intermediate geometric degree is \(\mathfrak d\), then localized generic slicing, multiplication matrices, and source-parametric identity testing return exactly \((d_e(G),p_e,\mathcal Q_{G,e},h_{G,e})\). Here \(p_e\in K_G[t]\) is the monic minimal polynomial of \(\lambda_e\), its coefficients and every member of \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\) are rational arithmetic circuits in the covariance entries, \(h_{G,e}\) is a nonzero product of the required localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-infinity, leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting factors, and \(\deg p_e=d_e(G)\leq2^{k+1}\). For universal constants \(a,b>0\), construction time and certificate length are bounded by
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{a}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)),
\]
with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\). In particular, if \(s,\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), the bound is \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) for a universal \(C\). The cited geometric-resolution algorithms begin with a reduced regular-sequence chart or a supplied lifting fiber; they neither select this source-prime chart from the extensional quadratic core nor perform the required descent from an unspecified embedded source component.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), \(r\leq2k\), denote the exposed coordinates on one recorded stratum, and use the notation \(J,H,P,h_1,\ldots,h_c,\Delta\) from the definition of a valid chart. Since
\[
 P K_G[x]_{H\Delta}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta}
\]
is reduced and prime and \(\Delta\) is nonzero at the source generic point, the Jacobian has rank \(c\) on a nonempty principal open subset of this chart. Its dimension is therefore \(d=r-c\). Adjoining \(z\) and
\[
 zH\Delta-1=0
\]
turns the localization into an affine system without deleting any point of the source-prime open set.

Choose \(d\) affine linear forms \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d\) with independently variable coefficients. Over \(\overline{K_G}\), the prime \(P\) has finitely many geometric components. Successive generic hyperplanes meet each nonempty component properly and reduce its dimension by one; the bad choices form a proper Zariski-closed subset of the coefficient space. Because \(\lambda_e\) is algebraic over \(K_G\), its conjugates form a finite set, and each conjugate occurs on at least one of these geometric components. Intersecting the finitely many nonempty open conditions on the slicing coefficients therefore gives a slice which is zero-dimensional, reduced, and meets a component carrying every conjugate of \(\lambda_e\).

Apply the cited geometric-resolution algorithms to the supplied reduced chart, its inequation, and this generic slice. Their arithmetic cost is polynomial in the chart straight-line-program length and the intermediate geometric degree. Let \(B\) be the resulting finite reduced \(K_G\)-algebra, after adjoining the recorded rational expression for \(\lambda_e\) if the query is not itself an exposed coordinate, and let \(M_e\) denote multiplication by that element. The characteristic polynomial \(\chi_e(t)=\det(tI-M_e)\) lies in \(K_G[t]\). Every geometric point of the slice lies on the source prime, so its queried coordinate is a root of the minimal polynomial \(p_e\); conversely, the generic-slice construction meets a component carrying each \(K_G\)-conjugate of \(\lambda_e\). Hence
\[
 \{z\in\overline{K_G}:\chi_e(z)=0\}
 =\{z\in\overline{K_G}:p_e(z)=0\}.
\]
Characteristic zero makes \(p_e\) separable. Both polynomials are monic, so taking the squarefree part of \(\chi_e\) gives exactly \(p_e\), rather than merely a polynomial having \(p_e\) as an unknown factor. Its degree is therefore \(d_e(G)\), and the established orientation bound gives \(d_e(G)\leq2^{k+1}\).

All input coefficients belong to \(K_G\) and are represented by rational covariance circuits. Fraction-free multiplication-matrix arithmetic therefore represents the coefficients of \(p_e\) by rational covariance circuits as well. Source substitution tests every proposed zero identity and every denominator or inequation for nonvanishing in \(L\). Homogenizing the sliced equations produces projective leading-form and infinity resultants; the multiplication polynomial produces its specialized leading-coefficient and squarefreeness resultants; the chart and reconstruction maps supply the covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, and zero-over-zero factors. The generic rational-univariate-specialization lemma shows that away from the product of these nonzero factors the computed finite coordinate set specializes without a degree drop or exchange with projective infinity. Applying the established real quantifier-elimination and algebraic-sampling procedures to the chart and its recorded reconstruction signs supplies the real-lifting factors and root certificates. Because at most \(2k\) exposed variables remain, these sign computations cost \((n+s)^{O(k+1)}\mathfrak d^{O(1)}\).

The remaining algebraic steps are matrix arithmetic of dimension at most the geometric degree, so for universal \(a>0\) the total construction and output size are bounded by
\[
 (n+s)^{a(k+1)}\mathfrak d^a\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta)).
\]
Allocate error probability \(\delta/M\) to each of the \(M\) source identity tests. The Schwartz--Zippel bound and a union bound give total symbolic error at most \(\delta\). If \(s,\mathfrak d\leq n^{b(k+1)}\), enlarging a universal constant gives the displayed \(n^{C(k+1)}\) bound.

Finally, the hypothesis is essential to this corollary. The Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy procedure assumes the reduced regular-sequence chart on the relevant open set, while the Lecerf lifting-fiber procedure accepts arbitrary equations and inequations only after the intended lifting fiber has been supplied. The extensional projection-preservation assertion for \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\) supplies neither object and does not imply that its displayed generators are reduced along \(P\). Thus the cited algorithms justify the computation after \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) is given, but they do not construct \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) or solve descent from an unspecified embedded component.
added_lemmas.justification: This is the strongest finite-output guarantee supported once the missing reduced source-prime chart is supplied explicitly.
added_lemmas.gap: Published geometric-resolution algorithms begin from a reduced chart or a supplied lifting fiber; they do not select the embedded source component represented only extensionally by the quadratic core.
added_lemmas.consumer: A future chart-selection theorem would discharge the antecedent and immediately provide the exact branch polynomial and its specialization certificates to fasttreeid.

added_lemmas.statement: Can one construct, uniformly from \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\), a valid source-prime chart package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) with size and intermediate geometric degree at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\), without a presentation, factorization, or component oracle for the embedded source prime? Equivalently, can the unconditional algebraic tag be strengthened, within \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) time and certificate length, to return the exact degree \(d_e(G)\), its monic minimal polynomial \(p_e\), the complete family \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and the nonzero bad-locus circuit \(h_{G,e}\), with total symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\)? A solution must prove source-prime chart selection and coefficient descent; generic radical decomposition, a generic rational univariate representation, or a lifting-fiber algorithm applied to the unseparated extensional core does not by itself answer the question.
added_lemmas.justification: Exact finite degree, eliminant, and bad-locus output remain the software-critical algorithmic gap after the unconditional rank decision is separated from component selection.
added_lemmas.gap: The extensional quadratic core does not supply a reduced local presentation, a source-nonzero Jacobian minor, or descent for the embedded source prime.
added_lemmas.consumer: Resolving this question would upgrade the unconditional fasttreeid extension from a finite/infinite tag to exact higher-degree branch certificates.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \((G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k}\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\), there is a universal \(C>0\) such that \(\mathsf A(G,T,e,\delta)\), with symbolic error probability at most \(\delta\), decides whether \(d_e(G)<\infty\). On the algebraic branch it returns only the tag \(\mathtt{algebraic}\), together with the already proved bound \(d_e(G)\leq 2^{k+1}\); it does not claim to construct \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). On the transcendental branch it returns exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) is a source-parametric rank certificate proving that the queried-coordinate morphism from the integral generic covariance fiber is dominant onto \(\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\). In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), its construction time and certificate length are at most \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The extensional quadratic core supports an unconditional algebraic-versus-transcendental rank test, but it does not supply the reduced source-prime chart required to construct the finite eliminant, its descent, or the complete exceptional-set certificate.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: In \(\mathsf{ArithmeticModel}\), form source-parametric circuits for the covariance Jacobian and for the same Jacobian augmented by the row of \(\lambda_e\). Use randomized source-parameter identity tests during fraction-free elimination to compare their generic ranks. If the ranks agree, return only the tag \(\mathtt{algebraic}\). If the augmented rank is larger, return exactly \((\infty,\mathcal N_{G,e})\), where \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) consists of the rank transcript and a source-nonzero augmented minor certifying dominance of the queried-coordinate projection. This unconditional construction does not return \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The unconditional construction can compare generic source-Jacobian ranks, but finite minimal-polynomial and exceptional-set construction requires the missing source-prime chart.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart package as in \(\mathrm{def:source\mbox{-}prime\mbox{-}chart}\), and successful output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\). Define \(\mathcal E_{G,e}=V(h_{G,e})=\{\Sigma:h_{G,e}(\Sigma)=0\}\), where \(h_{G,e}\) is the product of the nonzero covariance-localization, incidence-lifting, pole, projective-leading-form, specialized-leading-coefficient, squarefreeness, and real-lifting circuits returned by that conditional construction.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The circuit \(h_{G,e}\) is returned only by the conditional geometric-resolution construction.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Conditional on the source-prime chart hypothesis and successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) is a connected cell of a smooth semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathcal M_G\setminus\mathcal E_{G,e}\), refined by the signs used in \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\), on which the number and extendability labels of the simple real roots of \(p_e\) are constant.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The cell uses \(p_e\), \(h_{G,e}\), and lifting signs only after conditional finite-output construction.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Conditional on the source-prime chart hypothesis and successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), for fixed \(G,n,e\) with \(d_e(G)<\infty\), select \(\mathcal C_{G,e}\) as in \(\mathrm{def:regular\mbox{-}cell}\) and let \(\mathcal K_G\subset\mathcal C_{G,e}\) be any nonempty compact set with nonempty relative interior in that cell.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The compact inference class must inherit the condition under which its regular cell and certificate locus are available.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Conditional on the source-prime chart hypothesis and successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), if \(S_m\) lies in the tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\pi_G(S_m)\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\), and the supplied circuits evaluate validly, set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{z\in\mathbb R:p_e(\pi_G(S_m),z)=0\text{ and }\mathsf{LiftCert}(z,\pi_G(S_m))\text{ accepts}\}\), retaining every accepted branch and selecting none; otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The unconditional rank algorithm no longer returns the polynomial or lifting circuits consumed by this estimator.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Conditional on the source-prime chart hypothesis and successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), construct \(\mathcal A_m\) by mapping a joint Gaussian covariance ellipsoid for \(\pi_G(S_m)\) through every locally labeled component of \(r\), using the implicit derivative \(D r_j(\Sigma)[H]=-D_\Sigma p_e(\Sigma,r_j)[H]/\partial_t p_e(\Sigma,r_j)\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The implicit derivative is computable only after the conditional construction supplies rational circuits for \(p_e\).

proposed.name: Reduced source-prime chart package
proposed.construction:
For a source-consistent recorded stratum of \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\), where \(r\leq2k\), be its exposed coordinates, and let \(\xi:K_G[x]\to L\) be source evaluation. Let \(J\) be generated by the cleared core equations and the recorded factors whose images under \(\xi\) vanish, let \(H\) be the product of the recorded factors whose images under \(\xi\) are nonzero, and put \(P=\ker\xi\). A valid source-prime chart consists of \(c=\operatorname{ht}P\) circuit polynomials \(h_1,\ldots,h_c\in J\) and a \(c\)-by-\(c\) Jacobian minor \(\Delta\) such that \(\xi(H\Delta)\neq0\) and
\[
 P K_G[x]_{H\Delta}=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)K_G[x]_{H\Delta}
\]
is a reduced complete-intersection prime. A valid package \(\mathfrak C_{G,e}\) supplies such data for every source-consistent recorded stratum, together with the recorded rational reconstruction maps for all suppressed directed coefficients. Its size \(s\) is the total straight-line-program length, and its intermediate geometric degree \(\mathfrak d\) is the maximum degree of the localized varieties encountered after adjoining \(zH\Delta-1\), taking generic affine slices, and performing the recorded real-lifting sign computations.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The missing antecedent of exact finite-output construction must be defined explicitly and cannot be inferred from extensional projection preservation.

proposed.name: Conditional projected-covariance root-set estimator
proposed.construction: Conditional on the source-prime chart hypothesis and successful finite output of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\), if \(S_m\) lies in the tubular neighborhood of \(\mathcal K_G\), \(\pi_G(S_m)\notin\mathcal E_{G,e}\), and the supplied circuits evaluate validly, set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\{z\in\mathbb R:p_e(\pi_G(S_m),z)=0\text{ and }\mathsf{LiftCert}(z,\pi_G(S_m))\text{ accepts}\}\), retaining every accepted branch and selecting none; otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_{e,m}=\varnothing\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimator must consume the conditional certificate circuits directly rather than the narrowed unconditional algorithm.

On the algebraic branch it returns only the tag \(\mathtt{algebraic}\), together with the already proved bound \(d_e(G)\leq 2^{k+1}\); it does not claim to construct \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\). proposed.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser reports the corresponding faster implementation.

Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives graphical identifiability criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.

Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space. The unconditional theorem here gives a source-rank finite-versus-transcendental certificate on the tree-plus-excess class, but exact finite eliminant output remains conditional.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas, not algebraic coordinate minimal polynomials or branch degree.

Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric systems and controls specialization bad loci, but it does not select the SEM source-prime chart required by the conditional corollary.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The positioning must no longer describe the unconditional theorem as returning exact finite degrees and eliminants.

prose_updates.tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates a finite algebraic ambiguity regime not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object remains the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The paper proves the projection-aware upper bound and pursues the all-size attaining recurrence. Algorithmically, a source-Jacobian rank comparison gives an unconditional fixed-parameter finite-versus-transcendental tag and a dominance certificate. Exact finite degrees, minimal polynomials, bad-locus circuits, real lifting, and the regular finite-set inference rung are obtained conditionally when a bounded reduced chart of the embedded source prime is supplied; constructing that chart uniformly is a named open question rather than an implicit elimination step.

project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the projection-aware degree bound and all-size frontier program, proves an unconditional fixed-parameter algebraic-versus-transcendental rank certificate, and isolates the precise source-prime chart needed for exact finite eliminants. A conditional geometric-resolution theorem then yields the minimal polynomial, specialization and lifting circuits, and the regular finite-set inference interface, while a named open question records the missing uniform chart-selection and descent theorem.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\) and a valid bounded source-prime chart package has been supplied, project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the resulting regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the conditionally constructed certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. When \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the unconditional symbolic stage reports transcendence and the finite-set inference rung does not apply. Without the chart package, the unconditional finite tag does not by itself supply an estimator.

prose_updates.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree predicate in fasttreeid. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton exhibit higher-degree small SEMs, so novelty is not attached to a lone cubic or quartic. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz give a general polynomial-space generic identification decision, while Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different notion from algebraic branch degree. The unconditional theorem here is correspondingly limited to a parameterized source-rank finite-versus-transcendental tag. Corniquel and the geometric-resolution algorithms of Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy and Lecerf justify finite solving and specialization after a reduced regular-sequence chart or lifting fiber is supplied; they do not select the embedded SEM source prime from an extensional quadratic core or perform descent for an unspecified component. Exact degree, minimal-polynomial, and exceptional-set output is therefore stated as a conditional corollary plus an explicit open chart-selection question. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer and Mareis, Sturma, and Drton inform the downstream regular inference architecture, which is likewise conditional on those symbolic outputs.
prose_updates.interpretation: The unconditional certificate answers whether the queried edge has finite complex algebraic ambiguity or a Zariski-dense infinite coordinate image; it does not enumerate finite branches. A valid reduced source-prime chart upgrades the finite tag to the exact field degree and monic branch polynomial. Real roots are retained only after a supported real-extension test, and statistical neighborhoods cover all retained simple branches without selecting among them.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The quadratic core preserves the queried projection extensionally but does not present the reduced embedded source prime. Its displayed equations may vanish to higher order along that component, so source-parametric identity testing cannot manufacture a nonzero conormal Jacobian minor. General radical decomposition, a generic rational univariate representation, and lifting-fiber algorithms do not establish the required chart selection or coefficient descent in \(n^{C(k+1)}\) complexity. The orientation coefficient remains only an upper envelope until the separate all-size realization problem is solved. Coordinate localization is not promoted to full-fiber equality; real roots are not equated with real supported lifts; and local Jacobian rank is not used to claim real uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The all-size frontier recurrence and its attaining families remain the identification kernel. Unconditionally, the algorithmic contribution is a randomized exact source-Jacobian comparison returning either \(\mathtt{algebraic}\) with the established bound \(d_e(G)\leq2^{k+1}\), or \(\infty\) with a dominance certificate; it returns no finite degree, eliminant, or bad-locus circuit. Conditional on a supplied bounded reduced source-prime chart and source-nonzero Jacobian minor for every recorded stratum, localized geometric resolution returns \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and \(h_{G,e}\) with explicit dependence on chart size and intermediate geometric degree. Exceptional-set validity, real lifting, root-\(m\) finite-set inference, and singleton asymptotic normality are asserted only under that conditional symbolic output. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, all-singular-covariance guarantee, or inference from complex degree to real uniqueness is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The source-Jacobian rank comparison makes the finite-versus-transcendental status operational without presupposing a presentation of the embedded source prime.
statement_notes.gap: General polynomial-space identification and tree-only algorithms do not provide this parameterized source-rank certificate, while exact finite eliminant output remains the named chart-selection open question.
statement_notes.consumer: fasttreeid can extend its status layer to distinguish finite algebraic ambiguity from transcendence; exact higher-degree branch polynomials are available only through the conditional chart theorem.
